articles.title: ChatGPT: Memory Is a Cache, Custom Instructions Are Config (Where to Put Your Rules)
articles.excerpt: If you write software, you already know the difference between a config file and a cache. A config file is something you wrote, you can read it, and it behaves the same way every time. A cache is some…
articles.body: If you write software, you already know the difference between a config file and a cache. A config file is something you wrote, you can read it, and it behaves the same way every time. A cache is something the system fills in for itself, it changes as things change, and you should never trust it as your source of truth. That is the cleanest way I have found to explain ChatGPT custom instructions versus ChatGPT memory to people who keep seeing ChatGPT "remember" things and are not sure where it comes from. I checked the details below against OpenAI's Help Center in October 2026. Menus and limits vary by plan, so check your own Settings. Custom instructions: the config file Custom instructions are direct guidance you give about what ChatGPT should know and how it should answer.

articles.body: AI Productivity Myths: Lessons from the Real World #2 Why coding is not the bottleneck — and why speeding it up barely moves the needle on actual delivery. A few weeks ago I was at a company social event. It was one of those informal ones where people drift between conversations with drinks in hand. I expected the usual mix of project updates, football banter and weekend plans. What I got instead was wall-to-wall AI talk. More sort of personal kind. "What are you doing with it? What have you tried?" Nobody asked about the domain complexity I work in daily. The upstream dependencies we untangled that quarter — that was invisible. The architectural decision that saved us three months of rework did not even register as a topic worth raising. They wanted AI stories.

articles.title: Audit trail inmutable
articles.excerpt: Respuesta corta Un audit trail inmutable es un registro técnico que, una vez creado, no puede ser modificado ni eliminado, garantizando integridad, trazabilidad y verificabilidad de todas las operacio…
articles.body: Respuesta corta Un audit trail inmutable es un registro técnico que, una vez creado, no puede ser modificado ni eliminado, garantizando integridad, trazabilidad y verificabilidad de todas las operaciones en sistemas críticos. Su implementación efectiva requiere criptografía (hashes criptográficos, firmas digitales) y almacenamiento en entornos resistentes a la alteración (ej. blockchain permissioned o bases de datos append-only con control de acceso riguroso). TL;DR Un audit trail inmutable no permite ediciones, borrados ni sobrescrituras posteriores al registro inicial. La inmutabilidad se logra mediante técnicas criptográficas (hashes de cadena, firmas digitales) y arquitecturas de almacenamiento append-only .

articles.body: 之前一直写“零事故”，今天换个角度——把我会踩的坑先摘出来。折腾云服务器半年以上，最大的收获不是学会了多少命令，而是知道哪里会疼。三丰云这个 免费云服务器 ，我用它跑 Typecho + Nginx + 自动备份脚本，资源常年很轻松，但有几个设置不做好，后期真的很麻烦。 开机自启：别指望它能自己醒 我第一次部署完，重启机器发现博客挂了。Nginx 没设开机自启，Typecho 依赖的 PHP-FPM 也没跟着起。Linux 服务管理很直接， systemctl 或 chkconfig 都要手动配。 现在的做法是写个启动脚本，加入 rc.local 或者用 systemd 服务文件。每次开机，服务自动拉起，不用 SSH 进去手动敲命令。这一步做了，后续省掉很多“为什么挂了”的困惑。 备份清理：磁盘会涨，记得定期删 我观测到的情况是，磁盘每周涨几百 MB。原因很简单：Nginx 日志、Typecho 上传的图片、数据库备份文件。我的自动备份脚本每天跑一次，如果不加清理逻辑，一个月后磁盘就满了。 现在设定了保留策略：最近 7 天的备份保留，更早的每周清理一次。用 find 命令加上 -mtime 参数，配合 crontab 定时执行。磁盘空间从不满仓变成始终有余量，心态也稳。 提醒设置：续期靠自觉，但别忘了 这和上一篇文章里说的 7 天续期一样。我设了手机日历提醒，每周一早上弹一下。不只是续期，还有实例重启、证书更新这类琐事。没有提醒，大概率会忘；忘了，实例可能就被回收了。 数据方面，负载常年 0.2~0.5，内存占用不到一半。1 核 1G 的机器跑一个 Typecho 博客，确实绰绰有余。5M 带宽日常访问没问题，没遇到过限速或降权的情况。日志和流量统计对得上，没有暗扣。 为什么还愿意用这种“手动维护”的模式 自启配置一次，省去后续手动启动的麻烦 备份清理脚本自动化，磁盘空间可…

But there's just something about its narrow corridors and the threat of an undead monster popping out of a locker that keeps me from coming back to it. I've been playing Capcom's Switch 2 port of it lately, though, and I might finally make it to the end this time. The port is exquisite, and horrors on an 8-inch screen are much easier for my nerves to handle than big-screen frights.

articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look
articles.excerpt: The Orionids peak around Oct. 21. Here's when and where to look for the best chance of spotting meteors.
articles.body: If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing. Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22. So, when and where can you catch the show? articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 16, 1975: NASA launches the 1st-ever GOES weather satellite to watch Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES weather satellite. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES satellite! GOES-A was the first in a series of weather satellites that NASA jointly operated with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The name is short for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite . GOES-A launched on a Delta rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida. GOES satellites all have a geostationary orbit, which means they always face the same part of Earth — in this case, the Indian Ocean. Once GOES-A became operational, it was renamed GOES-1. The GOES satellite fleet has grown over the years, and is a critical link in the chain of satellites tracking Earth's weather from space.
